what_it_does: Creating 8K ultra-high-definition 60-frame-per-second video on edge devices (phones, cameras, edge servers) is challenging because it requires running a neural network (specifically, a space-time video super-resolution model—which intelligently fills in missing frame details and upscales low-res input) within tiny power and chip-area budgets. The bottleneck is moving intermediate data in and out of the on-chip memory (DRAM access burns 40–80% of energy). This chip (STEP) uses a technique called line-based depth-first fusion, which processes data in narrow horizontal strips rather than buffering entire feature maps, keeping more intermediate data on the fast on-chip cache. It also uses local caching of reused data and optimized global scheduling to minimize external memory trips while running 576 multiply-accumulate units (MAC—the basic math units that multiply and add numbers).
